newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK funds group drafting minimum trading standards.
newsitem.headline: HK funds group drafting minimum trading standards.

text.p: The Hong Kong Investment Funds Association (HKIFA) said on Friday it was drafting guidelines on personal account dealing by fund managers with the aim of putting in place a minumum standard of control.

Murray Simpson, chairman of the HKIFA's working group on internal control, told Reuters the effort was due to the diversity of the association's members, who have varying degrees of standards on personal account dealing.

"Some of our members' have controls which are significant and some members' controls are not so significant. These controls are done on an individual basis," said Simpson, who is managing director of Templeton Franklin Investment Services.
"We want to propose guidelines on minimum standards that would be put in place by our members to ensure the highest standards," he said.
The South China Morning Post reported on Friday that the HKIFA draft proposed guidelines effectively barring speculative personal account dealing by fund managers.

Client transactions would have to be satisfied before dealing for a personal account, and any potential conflict of interest would have to be reported to the compliance officer and appropriate senior director, the Post said.

Simpson said the Post report was correct in principle but stressed the draft proposal has not been finalised and some points could be changed, adding it was expected to be completed within the next month or so.
He added the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), Hong Kong's industry regulator, was looking into the proposals and will meet with the HKIFA next month.
